EE.Settings.HideDmTokens.Name: Hide DM-dropped tokens from players
EE.Settings.HideDmTokens.Hint: When you (the GM) drop a token onto a scene, make it invisible to players while still letting them target and interact with it. Toggle any single token from its HUD with the eye icon.
Make hidden tokens untouchable for players

Players can't hover, click, select, drag or box-select a token that's hidden from them, and can't nudge one with the arrow keys — as far as they can tell it isn't on the board at all. Targeting is unaffected, and so is anything that measures distance between tokens. Players still choose which of their own tokens is active from the Tokens on Scene bar.
EE.Settings.DisableDragAnimation.Name: Disable token drag animation
EE.Settings.DisableDragAnimation.Hint: Dragging and dropping a token moves it instantly instead of gliding it to the destination at Foundry's fixed animation speed. Applies to everyone at the table, and only to drag-and-drop — keyboard movement still animates.
EE.Settings.TokenBar.Name: Show players a "Tokens on Scene" bar
EE.Settings.TokenBar.Hint: Give each player a small floating list of the tokens they own on the current scene, so they can choose which one they're driving without hunting for it on the canvas — necessary when tokens are hidden from players. Players can drag the bar wherever they like; the GM never sees it.
EE.Settings.TokenBarLockSelection.Name: Never leave a player with nothing selected
EE.Settings.TokenBarLockSelection.Hint: If a player deselects their last token — by clicking empty ground, pressing Escape, or switching tools — put it straight back. Without this, their HUD falls back to whichever character it finds first, which may not be theirs.
EE.TokenBar.Title: Tokens on Scene
EE.TokenBar.SurveyTooltip: See what's on this scene and how far away it is
EE.TokenBar.SelectRefused: That token can't be selected right now. Switch back to the Select tool and try again.
EE.Settings.HotbarPageSwap.Name: Swap hotbar page on token selection
EE.Settings.HotbarPageSwap.Hint: Selecting a token switches the hotbar to the page assigned to that token's character. Nothing else in this window has any effect until this is on.
EE.Settings.RefreshRaisedPortraits.Name: Refresh raised portraits on artwork change
EE.Settings.RefreshRaisedPortraits.Hint: When a character's portrait image changes while Ginzzzu's Portraits is showing it, update the raised portrait to match instead of leaving the old artwork on screen. Portraits with a custom image or an active emotion are left alone.
EE.Settings.RollRequestClose.Name: Close the cinematic roll prompt after rolling
EE.Settings.RollRequestClose.Hint: When you request a roll in Cinematic Mode, close the player's prompt window once they've rolled instead of leaving it on screen over the result. Needs Daggerheart: Quick Actions.
EE.Settings.RollRequestOptions.Name: Let players choose advantage and Experiences on a roll request
EE.Settings.RollRequestOptions.Hint: Put Advantage/Disadvantage buttons and the character's Experiences (1 Hope each) on the roll request itself — on the cinematic prompt and on the whispered chat card — and roll it as the character the player is driving. Advantage or disadvantage you set in the request is shown but locked. Without this, a requested roll can't apply an Experience at all, and rolls with no character behind it for any player who has no assigned actor. Needs Daggerheart: Quick Actions.
EE.RollRequest.LockedByGm: Set by the GM for this roll.
EE.Settings.GeneralFeaturesMenu.Name: General Features
EE.Settings.GeneralFeaturesMenu.Label: Configure
EE.Settings.GeneralFeaturesMenu.Hint: Token visibility and selection, drag movement, and keeping raised portraits in step with character artwork.
EE.Settings.HotbarPagesMenu.Name: Per-Token Hotbars
EE.Settings.HotbarPagesMenu.Label: Configure Assignments
EE.Settings.HotbarPagesMenu.Hint: Choose which hotbar page each character switches to, and which page to fall back to for everything else.
EE.HotbarPages.Title: Per-Token Hotbars
EE.HotbarPages.Notes: Assign a character to a hotbar page and the bar switches to that page whenever one of its tokens is selected.
EE.HotbarPages.DefaultHint: Shown when an unassigned token is selected, or when nothing is selected at all.
EE.HotbarPages.ApplyToPlayersHint: Off by default: players keep their own macros on their own pages, so only your hotbar follows the selection.
EE.HotbarPages.NoActors: This world has no actors to assign.
EE.Settings.DaggerheartAutomationMenu.Hi: Apply Daggerheart rules the table would otherwise have to remember, and hook up Daggerheart-specific modules such as The Void.
EE.Settings.ReachMeleeAsVeryClose.Name: Reach
EE.Settings.ReachMeleeAsVeryClose.Hint: Give any character holding a feature called "Reach" — the Giant ancestry's — the range it describes: every weapon, ability, spell, or other feature of theirs with a Melee range works as though it were Very Close. Sheets, tooltips and target pickers all read the longer range. Nothing is saved to the cards themselves, so removing the feature (or this option) puts Melee straight back.
EE.Settings.AdaptabilityReroll.Name: Adaptability
EE.Settings.AdaptabilityReroll.Hint: Let a character holding the Human "Adaptability" feature use it: any roll that spent Hope on one of their own Experiences gets a "Mark a Stress to reroll" button on its chat card. The Stress is marked, the dice are thrown again on the same modifiers, and the card updates in place — including the Hope or Fear the first result had already given out. The button is withdrawn once the roll is a success the system can see; on a roll whose difficulty only the GM knows it stays available, because nothing here can tell whether it failed. Nothing happens unless the player presses it.
EE.Settings.FearlessFearToHope.Name: Fearless
EE.Settings.FearlessFearToHope.Hint: Let a character holding the Infernis "Fearless" feature use it: whenever they roll with Fear, offer to mark 2 Stress and turn it into a roll with Hope. Taking the offer converts the roll before anything reacts to the Fear — the GM gains no Fear, Fear countdowns don't advance, and other features that trigger on a Fear roll never fire. Declining, or letting the prompt time out, leaves the roll exactly as it landed.
EE.Settings.FelineInstinctsReroll.Name: Feline Instincts
EE.Settings.FelineInstinctsReroll.Hint: Let a character holding the Katari "Feline Instincts" feature use it: when an Agility roll comes up short, offer to spend 2 Hope and throw the Hope Die again. Only the Hope Die is rerolled — the Fear Die stays exactly as it landed — and the roll is re-scored from the new pair before anything acts on it, so the Hope or Fear, the countdowns and any hit all follow the second result rather than the first. The offer is only made on a roll the system scored as a miss; where the difficulty is the GM's to say out loud, nothing can tell whether it failed and no prompt is raised.
EE.Settings.BloodMaledictReroll.Name: Blood Maledict
EE.Settings.NotThisTimeReroll.Name: Not This Time
EE.Settings.StrangePatternsNumber.Name: Strange Patterns
EE.Settings.StrangePatternsNumber.Hint: Teach the Wizard's "Strange Patterns" feature when its number may be chosen. The system already matches the number against the Duality dice and hands out the Hope or the Stress clear — this governs the number itself: pressing the card chooses it while it is unset, the long rest dialog grows a control for changing it, and any other attempt to edit it is refused in between (the GM is never refused). Turning this off restores the card as it shipped, including the free Stress clear its "Clear Stress" button hands out.
EE.Settings.NotThisTimeReroll.Hint: Let a character holding the Wizard's "Not This Time" feature use it: whenever an adversary within Far range succeeds on an attack roll, or rolls damage, offer to spend 3 Hope and make it throw the dice again. The GM's client pauses the roll and puts the question on the character's owner's screen; taking it replaces the roll before the chat card is posted, so neither the original hit nor the original damage ever reaches anyone. The card's own "Spend Hope" button is left alone as the manual route. Needs both actors on the scene — a range that can't be measured raises no prompt.
EE.Settings.BloodMaledictReroll.Hint: Let a character holding the Void's "Blood Maledict" feature use it: whenever an adversary within Close range succeeds on an attack roll, offer to spend 3 Hope and make it reroll with disadvantage. The GM's client pauses the attack and puts the question on the character's owner's screen; taking it replaces the roll before the chat card is posted, so the original hit never becomes damage. Needs both actors on the scene — a range that can't be measured raises no prompt.
EE.Settings.CrimsonRiteEnchant.Name: Crimson Rite
EE.Settings.CrimsonRiteEnchant.Hint: Make the Void's "Crimson Rite" feature do what it says. Marking the Hit Point asks which active weapon to enchant (silently, if only one is equipped) and grants that weapon a tier-scaled bonus — 1d4 rising to 4d4 — which the system expires at the character's next rest, short or long. Using the feature again moves the rite rather than stacking it. The enchanted weapon's damage also counts as magic, which is the part the Void's own tier effects never managed on an ordinary physical weapon.
EE.Settings.BloodSpikeSpendHope.Name: Blood Spike
EE.Settings.BloodSpikeSpendHope.Hint: Resolve the Void's "Blood Spike" card in one press. Either of its attack actions now rolls the die the rule calls for — a d10 once the caster has 3 or more Hit Points marked, a d8 below that — so the d8 and d10 buttons stop being a choice you can get wrong, in either direction. On a hit, the caster is asked whether to spend the Hope: taking it rolls the damage as usual, declining rolls none, and the target marks its Stress either way (that part is already the card's own damage part, applied only to targets that were hit). A miss asks nothing. The card's separate "Spend Hope" action is left alone, as the manual route for a cast resolved without a target.
EE.Settings.BlightingStrikeDamage.Name: Blighting Strike
EE.Settings.BlightingStrikeDamage.Hint: Repair the shape of the Void's "Blighting Strike" card. It ships a Spellcast Roll that rolls no damage plus two separate damage actions, one for Hope and one for Fear, which you had to pick between by hand — and because a standalone damage action has no attack roll behind it, its damage never applied to anyone and a critical never maximised its dice. The card's own dice are moved onto the Spellcast Roll as a result-based damage part, d6+1 on a Hope result and d10+1 on a Fear one, and the two loose damage actions are removed. The system then rolls, scores and applies the whole card in one press. Nothing is written to the card — switch this off and it goes back exactly as it shipped. The card's "reduced by half" rider is automated too: a hit marks the target with a visible effect, and the next damage that creature deals to a Friendly token is halved, which clears the mark.
EE.Settings.HoldThemOffExtraTargets.Name: Hold Them Off
EE.Settings.HoldThemOffExtraTargets.Hint: Let a Ranger holding "Hold Them Off" use it: after a successful attack with a weapon, offer to spend 3 Hope and pick up to two more adversaries within the attack's range. Whoever is picked is added to the attack itself before the chat card is posted, so the one roll and the one damage roll resolve against all of them at once — hit or miss decided per adversary against their own Difficulty, exactly as if they had been targeted before the swing. The picker lists only adversaries the player can see and whose distance can be measured; it never shows anyone's Difficulty. Needs the attacker on the scene — a range that can't be measured raises no prompt, and neither does an unarmed strike or a Ranger below 3 Hope.
EE.Settings.RangersFocusTracking.Name: Ranger's Focus
EE.Settings.RangersFocusTracking.Hint: Make the Ranger's "Ranger's Focus" card do what it says, and enforce all three of its benefits. Press the card and it runs the whole thing in order: the Hope is spent, it asks which of your equipped weapons you're attacking with, then the attack picks its target from whoever is in that weapon's range (via Maiyalis: Target Helper, if you have it), and rolls — an ordinary attack, with its own dialog and damage. On a success the target becomes your Focus; on a miss the Hope is spent and nothing else happens, exactly as printed. You don't need to target anything first, and pressing it with nothing equipped refuses before the Hope is charged. The Focus is recorded as an effect on the ranger's own sheet, replacing any previous one — deleting it ends the feature — and the creature gets a matching label so you can see which token is being hunted. While it stands: any damage the ranger deals to their Focus also makes it mark a Stress, and a failed attack on the Focus offers to end the feature and reroll the Duality Dice, which is the only prompt that ever appears off an ordinary attack. Knowing what direction the Focus is in stays a conversation with the GM; it grants no number to apply.
EE.Settings.ISeeItComingEvasion.Name: I See It Coming
EE.Settings.ISeeItComingEvasion.Hint: Let a character holding the Bone domain's "I See It Coming" card use it: whenever an attack made from beyond Melee range lands on them, offer to mark a Stress, roll a d4 and add it to their Evasion against that attack. The attacker's client pauses the roll and puts the question on the character's owner's screen; taking it can turn the hit into a miss before the chat card is posted, so the hit never becomes damage. The d4 is posted to chat, whispered as far as the attack itself. Needs both actors on the scene — a range that can't be measured raises no prompt, and neither does an attack rolled against a fixed difficulty rather than Evasion.
EE.Settings.CompanionCommands.Name: Companion
EE.Settings.CompanionCommands.Hint: Put your animal companion's actions on the Beastbound "Companion" card, so commanding them starts where you'd look for it. As shipped that card is description-only: the rule — "Make a Spellcast Roll to connect with your companion and command them to take action" — lives on the companion's own sheet, where the attack button rolls as the companion, sending the Hope and Fear to an actor that has no Hope and leaving every bonus on your sheet out of it. With this on, the card offers two actions: your companion's attack, and a plain action roll for everything else. Both are your own Spellcast Roll — your trait, your bonuses, your Hope and Fear — and both offer your companion's Experiences for a Hope each, the way the card says. The attack keeps your companion's range, target and damage, and its range is measured from your companion's token rather than yours, so it can reach what it's standing next to (that last part needs Maiyalis: Target Helper, which is what gates range at all). On a success with Hope a note goes to chat reminding the table that your next action can gain advantage if it builds on their success — whether it does is the GM's call, so nothing is applied for you. Nothing is written to the card: switch this off, or unbind the companion, and it goes back to being description-only.
EE.Settings.CommuneOracle.Name: Commune
EE.Settings.CommuneOracle.Hint: Run the oracle on the Void's Witch class feature "Commune". As shipped, the card is description-only where it matters: pressing it spends your once-per-long-rest use and posts the chart, and everything after that — the dice, the choice, the answer — is left to the table. With this on, pressing it rolls a d6 for each point of your Spellcast trait (the same trait a Spellcast Roll uses, and the higher one if you're multiclassed) and throws them in chat where everyone can see them, then asks which of the rolled values you're keeping. Distinct values only: a pair of 4s is one choice, and a roll that came up all the same face still asks, showing its single option already chosen. A card then posts saying what that value bought — a flavor, a scent or a sensation on a 1-3; sounds or a vision on a 4-5; a scene experienced as if you were there on a 6 — and the GM is given a box to write the answer into, which lands in that same card. A GM who'd rather narrate it aloud can dismiss the box, and the card stands as rolled. The card's own use tracking is never touched, so switching this off returns the button to burning the use and posting the chart. Note the chart lives in this module rather than being read off the card, so a table that rewrote those three lines should leave this off.
EE.Settings.WitchsCharm.Name: Witch's Charm
EE.Settings.WitchsCharm.Hint: Make the Void's Witch class feature "Witch's Charm" do what it says. The card ships one action, "Spend Hope", and all it does is take 3 Hope — the conversion is left to the table, which by then means walking back the Hope the roller has already been given, handing the GM the Fear they haven't, and arguing with a chat card that has already printed a miss. With this on, a failed action roll pauses just before its card is posted and the question goes to every character within Far range who is holding this feature and has 3 Hope to spend, starting with the roller if it is theirs. Say yes and the roll becomes a success with Fear: the hit is re-decided, the Hope is not granted, the GM gains the Fear instead, and the card posts already reading that way — on every screen, and after a reload. They are asked one at a time and the first yes settles it, so two witches never pay for one rescue. Only a roll the system actually scored can be caught: an attack, or a check the GM entered a Difficulty for. A Difficulty kept in the GM's head leaves nothing to fail against, so nothing is offered, and the card's own button is still there to press by hand. Range is measured on the canvas the way the ruler measures it, so a scene where one of them has no token raises no prompt rather than guessing. Reaction rolls are left alone — they are not action rolls, which is why the system withholds Hope and Fear from them too.
EE.Settings.Hex.Name: Hex
EE.Settings.Hex.Hint: Make the Void's Witch class feature "Hex" do what it says. The card ships a "Mark Stress" action that charges the Stress and places an effect with no rules on it — which is not the Void's fault: "a bonus to rolls made against this creature" is a property of one roll, not of anybody's sheet, so no effect can express it. With this on, whenever a creature makes you or an ally within Close range mark Hit Points, the question goes to every character holding this feature who has a Stress to mark: hex the creature that did it, or let it be. Say yes and every action and damage roll aimed at that creature from then on gains your tier — the whole party's rolls, not only yours — shown as a named modifier in the roll dialog and in the card's breakdown, so nobody is left wondering where a number came from. The prompt waits half a minute and then lets the moment pass, and it only ever appears for damage that really marked Hit Points, so a hit soaked by armour or thresholds interrupts nobody. Hexing something else moves the condition, and the announcement card carries a button only you as GM can see: spend Fear equal to the witch's Spellcast trait to lift it, refused with the shortfall named when there isn't enough. "Remove it when the scene ends" is left to you — a scene is a fiction boundary, not a canvas or a combat, and guessing would lift a hex the table still counts. Delete the effect from the creature to end it. Reaction rolls gain nothing, since they are not action rolls, and healing never gains it at all.
EE.Settings.HerbalRemedies.Name: Herbal Remedies
EE.Settings.HerbalRemedies.Hint: Apply the Void's Hedge Witch subclass feature "Herbal Remedies" to consumables: when one clears Hit Points or Stress, it clears one more. The Void ships the card as prose and there is nothing else it could ship, because the rule fires on somebody else's button — whichever potion happens to get drunk. With this on, that extra point is added to the consumable's own formula before it is rolled, so a Minor Health Potion rolls 1d4 + 1 and the number the card prints is the number the sheet moves. That matters more than it sounds: a healing consumable declares no target, so nothing is ever applied automatically and the number is almost always marked off by hand. Hope and Armor Slots are left alone, since the card names Hit Points and Stress, and so is a consumable that clears a resource outright ("clear all HP and Stress"), which has no number to raise. "You or an ally" is read as: a character using a consumable, in a world where some character has this card. That is deliberately loose — the tighter readings all break at a table where the GM owns every sheet, or between sessions when nobody has a token on a scene — so a world holding both a Hedge Witch and a rival party who also drink potions should leave this off.
EE.Settings.TetheredTalisman.Name: Tethered Talisman
EE.Settings.TetheredTalisman.Hint: Make the Void's Hedge Witch subclass feature "Tethered Talisman" do what it says. The card ships a "Tether" action that spends its once-per-rest use, asks for a target and then does nothing at all: its effect list is empty. With this on, pressing it with one token targeted puts a talisman effect on that person, and from then on, whenever they would mark Hit Points, the question goes to you rather than to them — expend the talisman to mark one fewer, or save it. The reduction happens before anything is written to their sheet, which matters when the Hit Point in question is their last one. The prompt times out after half a minute and the damage lands as rolled, and it only ever appears when a live talisman is on the person who was actually hit, so nobody's turn is held up by a feature that is sitting idle. Spending the talisman removes it, which is what frees you to imbue another; so does deleting the effect from their sheet, which is how to call the whole thing off. Pressing the card while your last talisman is still out warns you first, and cancels the press if you decline, so nothing is spent by accident — the card's own once-per-rest bookkeeping is left entirely to the system. Only Hit Points are reduced: an attack that also marks Stress marks all of it, and one that marks Stress alone raises no prompt at all.
EE.Settings.BraveFace.Name: Brave Face
EE.Settings.BraveFace.Hint: Make the Void's Warborne community feature "Brave Face" do what it says. The card ships as description only, and the rule has no moment you could press it at: it fires inside somebody else's attack, after the damage is worked out and before your sheet is written. With this on, an attack that would make you mark a Stress asks you first — spend a Hope instead, or take the Stress. Say yes and the Stress is never marked at all, which is the whole point when your track is already full: the system turns an unmarkable Stress into a Hit Point, and this gets in ahead of that. The once-per-session use is a counter the module puts on the card itself, so you can see whether it's still there, and the system's own end-of-session refresh clears it — tick Session in the Daggerheart sidebar's refresh, the same button that clears everything else. An attack that would mark more than one Stress swaps one of them; the card says "a Stress". The prompt waits half a minute and then lets the attack through unchanged, and nothing is spent unless you say yes.
EE.Settings.CloseKnitShareHope.Name: Close-Knit
EE.Settings.CloseKnitShareHope.Hint: Put a "Share Hope" button on the Void's Hearthborne "Close-Knit" card, which ships as description only. Press it and you're asked who receives — every character assigned to a player, plus anyone standing on the current scene, each shown with the Hope they're already holding — and then how much of your own Hope to hand over. Nothing is spent until both questions are answered, so backing out of either costs you nothing. The Hope moves straight onto the other sheet, which needs a GM connected, the same as marking an adversary's Stress does. Using it puts a "Close-Knit (spent)" effect on your sheet that the system clears at your next long rest; delete it by hand to give the use back. Giving more Hope than an ally can hold spends all of it and says so — the card says any number, and the system caps every resource on the way in.
EE.Settings.AttackOfOpportunity.Name: Attack of Opportunity
EE.Settings.AttackOfOpportunity.Hint: Put an "Attack of Opportunity" button on the Warrior class feature, which the SRD ships as description only. It's a manual press rather than something watching the map: at a table where the GM shuffles tokens around to express positioning, a reaction that fired on every drag would be worse than one you ask for. Pressing it picks a target, then opens the system's own roll dialog — where the trait dropdown is how you choose which trait to roll, opened on your highest one — and scores the reaction roll against that target's Difficulty. On a success you're asked which of the card's three effects it bought, or two of them on a critical; choosing "deal damage" rolls your primary weapon's damage with no second roll to hit, since the reaction roll already landed. The other two effects are announced in chat and left to the table, because both are statements about the map. Nothing checks range: the card says Melee and the target picker marks the rows accordingly, but the fiction outranks the sketch.
EE.Settings.SlayerDice.Name: Slayer Dice
EE.Settings.SlayerDice.Hint: Run the dice pool on the Call of the Slayer subclass's "Slayer" card, which the SRD ships as description only. It puts a counter on the card in the Features tab, and does the four things the card asks for. On any roll with Hope, while there's still room on the card, you're offered a d6 in place of the Hope — the same prompt as any other feature reacting to that roll, and declining leaves the Hope exactly where it was. The attack and damage dialogs each gain a "Slayer Dice" dropdown listing however many you're holding; whatever you pick is rolled into the total, and the dice only leave the card once the roll actually happens, so backing out of a dialog costs you nothing. When you end the session from the Daggerheart sidebar tab with "Session" ticked, every unspent die is cleared and its holder gains a Hope for it, with a note in chat. A critical damage roll maximises spent Slayer Dice along with everything else in the roll, which is how the system already treats a Bardic Rally die. Switching this off stops all of it but leaves any dice already on a card alone.
EE.Settings.NotGoodEnoughReroll.Name: Not Good Enough
EE.Settings.NotGoodEnoughReroll.Hint: Let a character holding the Blade domain's "Not Good Enough" card use it: after they roll damage, any dice that came up 1 or 2 are offered back for a reroll. The offer arrives once the dice have landed on the table but before the result reaches the chat card, so the table reads one damage figure rather than watching it get corrected. Dice that were rerolled keep their old face on the card, struck through, and can never be rerolled a second time — the same bookkeeping the system's own per-die reroll button uses. Only the damage itself is offered; Stress, healing and other resource dice on the same action are left as they fell. Each player decides separately whether they want to be asked every time or just have it done, in their own module settings.
EE.Settings.NotGoodEnoughAlwaysReroll.Hi: Skip the "Not Good Enough" prompt and just reroll the 1s and 2s. This one is yours alone — it changes nothing for anyone else at the table, and it does nothing unless your GM has the card's automation switched on. Ticking "Always reroll 1s and 2s" on the prompt itself turns this on too.
EE.Settings.GiftedTrackerEvasion.Name: Gifted Tracker
EE.Settings.GiftedTrackerEvasion.Hint: Make the Sage domain's "Gifted Tracker" card grant its Evasion bonus the way it's written, against the creatures you tracked rather than against everything. As shipped the card applies a flat, permanent +1 Evasion to whoever you have targeted, which is wrong twice over — it never expires and it applies to every attack in the game. With this on, that effect is suppressed and replaced: press the card, spend as much Hope as you like (the system's own prompt), then say what you're following — "three sets of clawed prints, heading north" — and the GM is shown your description alongside a searchable list of every creature on the scene, in the world, and in every Actor compendium you have installed. Whatever the GM picks is recorded on your sheet as an effect naming your quarry, and from then on any attack one of those creatures makes against you is resolved against +1 Evasion, before the chat card is posted — so it can turn a hit into a miss, and it says so in chat when it does. Only one quarry at a time: using the card again on fresh tracks ends the previous tracking and says so in chat. Nothing else ends it automatically — losing the trail is a call for the table, made by deleting the effect from the sheet. Matching is by compendium entry, actor and name together, so picking one statblock covers every token of it. Note the bonus is applied to adversary attacks; a creature built on a character sheet rolls Duality instead and isn't covered.
EE.Settings.ViciousEntangleRestrain.Name: Vicious Entangle
EE.Settings.ViciousEntangleRestrain.Hint: Automate the Sage domain's "Vicious Entangle" card. Two things change. Pressing the card no longer asks which of its two actions you meant — it goes straight to the Spellcast Roll, and the damage and the Restrained effect on your target stay exactly as the card ships them. Then, on a success, the card's second sentence is offered where the rule actually allows it: every other adversary within Very Close range of whoever you hit, nearest first, each row naming the target it is standing beside. Pick one and they are Restrained and the Hope is spent — both read off the card itself, so a house-ruled cost or a swapped effect is honoured, and a line in chat says what it cost. Declining or dismissing the picker costs nothing. Nothing is offered on a miss, on a cast with no target, to a caster who cannot pay, or to an adversary whose distance cannot be measured — a Hope should not be spent on an assumed range, and the card's own "Restrain Another" button is still there for those cases. The picker lists only adversaries the player can see.
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormPortrait.Name: Sync portrait to Hybrid Form
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormPortrait.Hint: When The Void puts an Order of the Lycan character into Hybrid Form, change the character sheet portrait to match the transformed token art, and change it back when the form is dropped.
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormPrototype.Name: Also transform the prototype token
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormPrototype.Hint: Additionally rewrite the character's prototype token, so a token dragged onto a scene mid-transformation arrives in Hybrid Form. Off by default: unlike the portrait, this changes saved character data.
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormStressRevert.N: End Hybrid Form when Stress is full
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormStressRevert.H: When an Order of the Lycan character's Stress reaches its maximum while transformed, automatically revert them to human form, the same way clicking the wolf button would. Complements The Void's own rule that gaining Hope while transformed also marks Stress, which it never reverts the form for.
EE.GeneralFeatures.Title: General Features
EE.GeneralFeatures.QuickActionsMissing: Daggerheart: Quick Actions isn't active, so there are no roll requests to change. Enable it to use these.
EE.Automation.Title: Daggerheart Automation
EE.Automation.VoidRequired: Requires The Void (Unofficial), which is not installed or not enabled.
EE.Automation.VoidMissing: The Void (Unofficial) is not installed or not enabled, so its content below can't be configured.
EE.Features.DualityIntro: Hope {hope} vs Fear {fear} — a roll with {result}.
EE.Features.Adaptability.Title: Adaptability
EE.Features.Adaptability.Intro: That roll used {experience} and failed. You can mark a Stress to reroll it, keeping every bonus.
EE.Features.Adaptability.Tooltip: Adaptability — reroll this, keeping every bonus including the Experience.
EE.Features.Adaptability.Announce: {actor} marks a Stress and rerolls — Adaptability.
EE.Features.Adaptability.NoStress: {actor} has no Stress left to mark.
EE.Features.FelineInstincts.Title: Feline Instincts
EE.Features.FelineInstincts.Intro: That Agility roll missed with a total of {total}. You can spend 2 Hope to throw the Hope Die again — it is showing {hope}, and the Fear Die ({fear}) stays as it landed.
EE.Features.Fearless.Label: Fearless
EE.Features.Fearless.Hint: Mark 2 Stress to change this into a roll with Hope instead.
EE.Features.WitchsCharm.Title: Before the roll resolves
EE.Features.WitchsCharm.Label: Witch's Charm
EE.Features.WitchsCharm.Hint: Spend 3 Hope to make {roller}'s roll a success with Fear instead. The GM gains the Fear.
EE.Features.WitchsCharm.HintSelf: Spend 3 Hope to make this a success with Fear instead. You gain no Hope from it, and the GM gains the Fear.
EE.Features.WitchsCharm.Spent: {witch} spends 3 Hope — Witch's Charm. {roller}'s roll succeeds, with Fear.
EE.Features.Hex.Title: Before the moment passes
EE.Features.Hex.Label: Hex
EE.Features.Hex.Hint: Mark a Stress to Hex {attacker}. Every action and damage roll against it — anyone's, not only yours — gains +{tier}.
EE.Features.Hex.EffectDescription:
Action and damage rolls against this creature gain a bonus equal to the hexing Witch's tier.

Delete this effect when the scene ends, or spend Fear equal to her Spellcast trait to lift it early.
EE.Features.Hex.Announce: {witch} marks a Stress — Hex. {creature} is Hexed.
EE.Features.Hex.LiftButton: Spend {price} Fear to lift the Hex
EE.Features.Hex.LiftTooltip: The GM may spend Fear equal to the Witch's Spellcast trait to remove this condition.
EE.Features.Hex.LiftGone: That Hex names a creature or a Witch who is no longer here. Nothing was spent.
EE.Features.Hex.LiftAlready: {creature} is not Hexed any more. Nothing was spent.
EE.Features.Hex.LiftNoTrait: {witch} has no Spellcast trait, so the rule names no price. Delete the effect from the creature to lift the Hex.
EE.Features.Hex.LiftNoFear: Lifting this Hex costs {price} Fear, and there is {fear}. Nothing was spent.
EE.Features.Hex.Lifted: {price} Fear is spent: {witch}'s hex on {creature} is lifted.
EE.Features.BraveFace.Title: Brave Face
EE.Features.BraveFace.Intro: {attacker}'s attack would make you mark a Stress.
EE.Features.BraveFace.IntroMany: {attacker}'s attack would make you mark {marks} Stress. Brave Face covers one of them.
EE.Features.BraveFace.Label: Spend a Hope instead
EE.Features.BraveFace.Hint: Once per session. You are holding {hope} Hope.
EE.Features.BraveFace.Announce: {actor} puts on a brave face — spending a Hope rather than marking a Stress from {attacker}.
EE.Features.AwaitingReaction: Waiting for {user} to answer a reaction prompt…
EE.Features.AdversaryAttackIntro: {attacker} succeeded on an attack roll, hitting {targets}.
EE.Features.BloodMaledict.Label: Blood Maledict
EE.Features.BloodMaledict.Hint: Spend 3 Hope to make them reroll this attack with disadvantage.
EE.Features.NotThisTime.Label: Not This Time
EE.Features.NotThisTime.AttackHint: Spend 3 Hope to make them reroll this attack.
EE.Features.NotThisTime.DamageHint: Spend 3 Hope to make them reroll this damage.
EE.Features.StrangePatterns.Title: Strange Patterns
EE.Features.StrangePatterns.ChooseIntro: Choose a number between 1 and 12. When you roll that number on a Duality Die, gain a Hope or clear a Stress.
EE.Features.StrangePatterns.ChangeIntro: Choose the number you will watch for until your next long rest.
EE.Features.StrangePatterns.Announce: {actor} is watching for {number} on the Duality dice.
EE.Features.StrangePatterns.AnnounceChan: {actor} is watching for {number} on the Duality dice, instead of {previous}.
EE.Features.StrangePatterns.Reminder: You are watching for {number}. The number changes when you take a long rest.
EE.Features.StrangePatterns.Locked: Strange Patterns is watching for {number}. The number can only change during a long rest.
EE.Features.StrangePatterns.RestSet: The number you are watching for.
EE.Features.ISeeItComing.Label: I See It Coming
EE.Features.ISeeItComing.Hint: Mark a Stress to roll a d4 and add it to your Evasion against this attack.
EE.Features.ISeeItComing.Flavor: I See It Coming — Evasion {before} → {after} against this attack.
EE.Features.CrimsonRite.ChooseIntro: Which of your active weapons does the rite enchant?
EE.Features.CrimsonRite.Applied: Crimson Rite: {weapon} deals an extra {formula} magic damage until your next rest.
EE.Features.CrimsonRite.NoWeapon: Crimson Rite needs an equipped weapon to enchant, and you have none.
EE.Features.CrimsonRite.Unequipped: Crimson Rite ended — the weapon it enchanted is no longer equipped in that slot.
EE.Features.BlightingStrike.MarkDescript: The next time this creature deals damage to a friendly target, that damage is reduced by half. Removed automatically when it happens.
EE.Features.BloodSpike.Title: Blood Spike
EE.Features.BloodSpike.Label: Spend a Hope
EE.Features.BloodSpike.Hint: Deal the spike's magic damage, rolling {die}. Decline and it deals none — the target marks its Stress either way.
EE.Features.BloodSpike.HintEscalated: Deal the spike's magic damage. You have {marks} Hit Points marked, so the die is {die}. Decline and it deals none — the target marks its Stress either way.
EE.Features.BloodSpike.NoHope: Blood Spike hit, but you have no Hope to spend — the target marks a Stress and takes no damage.
EE.Features.HoldThemOff.Title: Hold Them Off
EE.Features.HoldThemOff.Intro: Your {weapon} hit {targets}. Spend {hope} Hope to catch up to two more adversaries within {range} with the same roll.
EE.Features.HoldThemOff.IntroNoTarget: Your {weapon} attack succeeded. Spend {hope} Hope to catch up to two adversaries within {range} with the same roll.
EE.Features.RangersFocus.Title: Ranger's Focus
EE.Features.RangersFocus.ChooseWeapon: Which weapon do you make the attack with?
EE.Features.RangersFocus.TargetEffectDes: This creature is a ranger's Focus. While it lasts, they know precisely what direction it is in, and any damage they deal it also makes it mark a Stress.
EE.Features.RangersFocus.NoWeapon: Ranger's Focus needs an equipped weapon to attack with, and you have none. No Hope has been spent.
EE.Features.RangersFocus.NoWeaponChosen: Ranger's Focus: no weapon chosen, so no attack was made — the Hope has been spent.
EE.Features.RangersFocus.RerollIntro: Your attack on {target}, your Focus, missed. End Ranger's Focus to reroll your Duality Dice?
EE.Features.RangersFocus.EffectDescripti:
Until this feature ends or you make a different creature your Focus:

  • You know precisely what direction they are in.

  • When you deal damage to them, they must mark a Stress.

  • When you fail an attack against them, you can end this feature to reroll your Duality Dice.

Delete this effect to end the feature.
EE.Features.RangersFocus.Missed: {ranger}'s Ranger's Focus attack missed — the Hope is spent and no Focus is made.
EE.Features.RangersFocus.Ended: {ranger} ends Ranger's Focus on {target} to reroll.
EE.Features.TetheredTalisman.Title: Tethered Talisman
EE.Features.TetheredTalisman.NoTarget: Tethered Talisman needs exactly one target — whoever will be carrying it. Target a token (your own, if you're keeping it yourself) and press the card again. Nothing has been spent.
EE.Features.TetheredTalisman.EffectDescr:
A small item imbued with a Hedge Witch's protective essence. The next time you would mark Hit Points, she may expend it to make you mark one fewer.

Delete this effect to give the talisman up; she can then imbue another.
EE.Features.TetheredTalisman.ReplaceIntr: Your talisman is already out — {holder} is carrying it. Imbuing a new one cancels it.
EE.Features.TetheredTalisman.ReplaceConf: Cancel it and imbue a new one
EE.Features.TetheredTalisman.Intro: {holder} is about to mark {marking} Hit Point(s), and is carrying your talisman. Expending its magic brings that down to {reduced}.
EE.Features.TetheredTalisman.OfferHint: Expend the talisman's magic for one fewer Hit Point. It is used up — and you can imbue another.
EE.Features.TetheredTalisman.Spent: {witch}'s talisman is expended: {holder} marks one less Hit Point.
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.Label: Gifted Tracker
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.Hint: You have tracked this creature: +1 Evasion against it.
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.Title: Gifted Tracker
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.Describe: What are you following? Describe the signs of their passage — the GM will tell you what left them, and answer {hope} question(s).
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.DescribePlaceh: Three sets of clawed prints in the mud, heading north…
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.NoDescription: Gifted Tracker: nothing was described, so no tracking was recorded — the Hope has been spent.
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.Sent: Gifted Tracker: your description has gone to the GM.
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.GmIntro: {name} is tracking something, and spent {hope} Hope to ask about it. Which creatures left these signs?
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.NothingRecorde: Gifted Tracker: no creatures were named, so nothing was recorded.
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.EffectDescript: You are tracking {names}. You gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion against them. Delete this effect when you stop tracking them — using Gifted Tracker again on a new quarry also ends it.
EE.Features.GiftedTracker.Evaded: {attacker} misses {name}, who has tracked them — Evasion {before} → {after}.
EE.Features.ViciousEntangle.Title: Vicious Entangle
EE.Features.ViciousEntangle.Intro: Your vines have {targets} Restrained. Spend {cost} to catch one more adversary within {range} of them.
EE.Features.ViciousEntangle.CannotPay: Vicious Entangle: you no longer have {cost} to spend, so nothing was entangled.
EE.Features.ViciousEntangle.Announced: {name} spends {cost}; the vines catch {target}, who is Restrained.
EE.Features.Commune.Title: Commune
EE.Features.Commune.Sensation: You taste a flavor, smell a scent, or feel a sensation relevant to the answer.
EE.Features.Commune.Vision: You hear sounds or see a vision relevant to the answer.
EE.Features.Commune.Scene: You psychically experience a scene relevant to the answer as if you were there.
EE.Features.Commune.GmIntro: {name} communed and kept a {value}. {effect} What comes through?
EE.Features.Commune.AnswerPlaceholder: Wet stone, and a bell tolling somewhere far below…
EE.Features.Commune.Sent: Commune: the GM has been asked what comes through.
EE.Features.Commune.NothingWritten: Commune: nothing was written down, so the card stands as rolled.
EE.Features.Commune.NoTrait: Commune rolls a d6 for each point of your Spellcast trait, and yours is not above zero — there are no dice to roll.
EE.Features.Companion.AttackHint: {companion} attacks. You make the Spellcast Roll; spend a Hope to add one of their Experiences. The attack reaches from where {companion} is standing, not from you.
EE.Features.Companion.CommandHint: Connect with {companion} and command them to take action. Make a Spellcast Roll against a difficulty the GM sets; spend a Hope to add one of their Experiences.
EE.Features.Companion.HopeReminder: {companion} succeeded with Hope — if your next action builds on their success, you gain advantage on the roll.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.Title: Close-Knit
EE.Features.CloseKnit.ActionHint: Spend any number of Hope to give an ally the same number of Hope. Once per long rest.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.AllyIntro: Who receives your Hope? You are holding {hope}.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.AmountIntro: How much goes to {ally}? They are holding {hope} of {max}.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.Wasted: {count} of it had nowhere to go: {ally} was already holding all the Hope they can.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.SpentEffectDescrip: Close-Knit has been used since your last long rest. This clears at the next one — or delete it to hand the use back.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.Spent: {actor} has already used Close-Knit since their last long rest.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.NoHope: Close-Knit gives away Hope, and {actor} has none to give.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.NoAlly: Close-Knit needs an ally to receive the Hope, and there is nobody else here.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.NoGM: Close-Knit moves Hope between two sheets, which needs a GM connected. Nobody is.
EE.Features.CloseKnit.NoActor: Close-Knit belongs to a character, and this card is on nobody's sheet.
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.Title: Attack of Opportunity
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.ActionHi: An adversary is leaving Melee range. Make a reaction roll with a trait of your choice against their Difficulty, then choose one effect — or two on a critical success.
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.IntroOne: Your reaction roll beat {target}'s Difficulty. Choose one effect.
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.IntroTwo: Critical success against {target}. Choose up to two effects.
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.EffectHo: They can't move from where they are.
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.EffectDa: You deal damage to them equal to your primary weapon's damage.
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.ConfirmE: You haven't chosen an effect. Take nothing from this Attack of Opportunity?
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.Announce: {actor} catches {target} leaving Melee range — a critical success, so two effects.
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.NoTarget: Attack of Opportunity is rolled against an adversary's Difficulty, and nobody was targeted.
EE.Features.AttackOfOpportunity.NoDamage: {actor} has no primary weapon damage to deal.
EE.Features.Slayer.Label: Slayer
EE.Features.Slayer.Hint: Place a d6 on the card instead of gaining the Hope.
EE.Features.NotGoodEnough.Title: Not Good Enough
EE.Features.NotGoodEnough.Intro: You rolled a 1 or 2 on your damage dice. Would you like to reroll?
EE.Features.NotGoodEnough.Always: Always reroll 1s and 2s for damage rolls?
EE.Features.NotGoodEnough.Remembered: Not Good Enough will reroll 1s and 2s without asking. Turn it off again in Configure Settings.
EE.Picker.NoMatches: Nothing matches. Try a shorter search.
EE.Picker.More: …and {count} more. Narrow the search to see them.
EE.Picker.NothingChosen: Nothing chosen yet — search above, then click to add.
EE.Settings.DaggerheartUtilitiesMenu.Hin: Table rules for Daggerheart play, such as capping how many decks are in play at once.
EE.Settings.RelayActionEffects.Name: Let players apply action effects to adversaries
EE.Settings.RelayActionEffects.Hint: When a Daggerheart action applies an effect to a target the acting player does not own, ask the active GM's client to apply the original effect. This covers effects such as temporary Vulnerable on a successful hit; it does not relay arbitrary effect creation.
EE.ActionEffectRelay.NoGM: An active GM must be connected to apply this effect to that target.
EE.ActionEffectRelay.Disabled: The GM has disabled relaying action effects to targets players do not own.
EE.ActionEffectRelay.Unauthorized: The GM rejected this action effect because you do not own its source actor.
EE.ActionEffectRelay.Invalid: The GM could not verify the source effect or its target.
EE.ActionEffectRelay.Failed: The action effect could not be applied by the GM.
EE.Settings.DeckLimitEnabled.Name: Limit the number of decks
EE.Settings.DeckLimitEnabled.Hint: Cap how many decks can be in play at once. Off by default — nothing is limited until you turn this on.
EE.Settings.DeckLimitCount.Name: Number of decks
EE.Settings.DeckLimitCount.Hint: How many decks the limit above allows. Minimum 1.
EE.Settings.DeckLimitPlayersOnly.Name: Only limit player characters
EE.Settings.DeckLimitPlayersOnly.Hint: Count and restrict only characters assigned to (or owned by) a player. Your own character sheets — pregens, test characters, retired PCs — stay out of the pool entirely: they don't use up copies, and they aren't blocked from taking any. Off by default, where every character in the world draws from the decks.
EE.Utilities.Title: Daggerheart Utilities
EE.Utilities.DeckContentsHint: Copies of each card a single deck contains, multiplied by the number of decks above to get the pool. The defaults match a printed Daggerheart deck — change them if your table proxies or homebrews extra cards. Zero means a deck holds none of that card type.
EE.DeckLimit.OnHoldBy: On hold: {holders} — picked but not yet confirmed.
EE.DeckLimit.HeldByNobody: Nobody is holding it — the deck simply doesn't contain one.
EE.DeckLimit.BlockedBody: All {pool} copies of {name} are already in play, so there isn't one left to take.
EE.DeckLimit.BlockedAsk: If you need it anyway, ask your GM — they can add it for you.
EE.DeckLimit.ExceedBody: All {pool} copies of {name} are already in play. Adding this one puts more copies on the table than the decks hold.
EE.DeckLimit.ExceedHint: You're the GM, so this is allowed — this is only a check that you meant it.
EE.DeckLimit.TooltipNone: Deck limit — the deck holds none of these
EE.DeckLimit.TooltipOnHold: On hold by {holders} — picked in an open character creation or level-up, but not confirmed yet
EE.Settings.SessionLogMenu.Name: Session Log
EE.Settings.SessionLogMenu.Label: Configure Log
EE.Settings.SessionLogMenu.Hint: Keep a running log of what happens during the session, for combining with the Discord voice transcript afterward to draft session notes.
EE.Settings.SessionLogEnabled.Name: Enable Session Log
EE.Settings.SessionLogEnabled.Hint: Start recording notable session events to the log. Off by default.
EE.Settings.SessionLogRolls.Name: Log dice rolls
EE.Settings.SessionLogRolls.Hint: Record each Duality/reaction roll's result — the total and whether it came up Hope, Fear, or a Critical Success.
EE.Settings.SessionLogResources.Name: Log resource changes
EE.Settings.SessionLogResources.Hint: Record Hit Point, Stress, Armor, and Hope changes as they happen.
EE.Settings.SessionLogStatus.Name: Log status changes
EE.Settings.SessionLogStatus.Hint: Record conditions and other effects gained or lost, and when a character goes down.
EE.Settings.SessionLogCombat.Name: Log combat
EE.Settings.SessionLogCombat.Hint: Record when combat begins and ends.
EE.Settings.SessionLogScenes.Name: Log scene changes
EE.Settings.SessionLogScenes.Hint: Record when you activate a different scene.
EE.Settings.SessionLogFlags.Name: Log GM flags
EE.Settings.SessionLogFlags.Hint: Record moments you flag manually from the chat log button.
EE.SessionLog.Title: Session Log
EE.SessionLog.ExportHint: Export the most recent session's entries to a page in the "Session Logs" journal, in the "Utility Suite" folder. Completed sessions are also exported automatically the next time something is logged after a 12-hour gap.
EE.SessionLog.ExportEmpty: There's nothing in the Session Log to export yet.
EE.SessionLog.Exported: Session exported to the "Session Logs" journal.
EE.SessionLog.FlagButton: Flag this moment for the session log
